about: A directory that POINTS to courts, official portals, published rules, law reports and legal aid bodies. It is not legal advice and it reproduces no court's or publisher's text. Descriptions are short general descriptions written for VIDHI; they have NOT been reviewed by a lawyer. The names, powers and money limits of subordinate and revenue courts differ from State to State: check the State's own law. A link is shown only after scripts/legal_directory_refresh.py found the address working; see the date beside it.

entries.name: Supreme Court of India
entries.what: The highest court of India. It hears appeals from the High Courts and tribunals and some matters directly.

entries.name: High Courts
entries.what: The highest court of a State or group of States and Union Territories. There are 25 High Courts; each one's own website is listed under High Court websites.

entries.name: District and Sessions Court
entries.what: The main court of a district. As District Judge it is the principal civil court of the district; as Sessions Judge it tries the more serious criminal cases. Additional District and Sessions Judges sit in the same court.
entries.law: Constitution of India, Article 233 (appointment of district judges); the State's Civil Courts Act; Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023
entries.note: Case status and orders of district and taluka courts are searched on the eCourts services site.

entries.name: Civil Judge (Senior Division)
entries.what: A civil court below the District Judge. Which suits it can hear, and up to what value, is fixed by the State's own Civil Courts Act.
entries.law: The State's Civil Courts Act; Code of Civil Procedure, 1908
entries.note: Called Subordinate Judge or Senior Civil Judge in some States.

entries.name: Civil Judge (Junior Division) / Munsif
entries.what: The first level of regular civil court. In some States this court is called the Munsif's court or Junior Civil Judge.
entries.law: The State's Civil Courts Act; Code of Civil Procedure, 1908

entries.name: Chief Judicial Magistrate
entries.what: The senior judicial magistrate of a district. Criminal cases that are not tried by the Sessions Court are tried by judicial magistrates.
entries.law: Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (before 1 July 2024: Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973)

entries.name: Judicial Magistrate of the First Class
entries.what: A criminal court below the Chief Judicial Magistrate. The classes of magistrates and the sentences each may pass are set out in the criminal procedure law.
entries.law: Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (before 1 July 2024: Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973)

entries.name: Judicial Magistrate of the Second Class
entries.what: A criminal court with lesser sentencing powers than a Magistrate of the First Class.
entries.law: Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (before 1 July 2024: Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973)
entries.note: Magistrates of the Third Class existed under the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898 and were not continued in the 1973 Code. There is no such class today.

entries.name: Executive Magistrates
entries.what: Officers of the administration (such as the District Magistrate and Sub-Divisional Magistrate) who have preventive and public-order powers under the criminal procedure law. They are not judicial courts.

entries.name: Small Cause Courts
entries.what: Courts for civil suits of small value, heard by a quicker procedure.
entries.law: Presidency Small Cause Courts Act, 1882; Provincial Small Cause Courts Act, 1887

entries.name: Family Courts
entries.what: Courts for disputes about marriage, maintenance, custody and related family matters.

entries.name: Commercial Courts
entries.what: Courts and High Court divisions for commercial disputes above a set value.

entries.name: Gram Nyayalayas
entries.what: Village-level courts for some civil and criminal matters, where a State has set them up.

entries.name: Lok Adalat
entries.what: A forum where a pending or pre-litigation dispute is settled by agreement. An award of a Lok Adalat is treated as a decree of a civil court. Permanent Lok Adalats deal with public utility services.

entries.name: Board of Revenue
entries.what: In States that have one, the highest revenue court of the State for land revenue matters. Some States have a Revenue Tribunal or a Financial Commissioner instead.
entries.note: Revenue courts decide land records, mutation, partition of holdings and similar matters under the State's land revenue law. Their names and the route of appeal differ in every State.

entries.name: Divisional Commissioner
entries.what: The revenue officer in charge of a division (a group of districts), who hears revenue appeals in many States.

entries.name: Collector (District Collector / Deputy Commissioner)
entries.what: The head of revenue administration in a district, who also sits as a revenue court.

entries.name: Sub-Divisional Officer / Assistant Collector
entries.what: The revenue officer of a sub-division, between the Collector and the Tehsildar.

entries.name: Tehsildar (Tahsildar / Mamlatdar)
entries.what: The revenue officer of a tehsil or taluka, usually the first revenue court for land record matters.

entries.name: Naib Tehsildar / Deputy or Assistant Tehsildar
entries.what: The officer below the Tehsildar, with the revenue powers the State's law gives.

entries.name: National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT)
entries.what: Company law and insolvency matters.

entries.name: National Company Law Appellate Tribunal (NCLAT)
entries.what: Appeals from the NCLT and some other bodies.

entries.name: Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT)
entries.what: Appeals in income-tax matters.

entries.name: Customs, Excise and Service Tax Appellate Tribunal (CESTAT)
entries.what: Appeals in customs, excise and service tax matters.

entries.name: Goods and Services Tax Appellate Tribunal (GSTAT)
entries.what: Appeals in goods and services tax matters.
entries.law: Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017

entries.name: Central Administrative Tribunal (CAT)
entries.what: Service matters of central government employees.

entries.name: Armed Forces Tribunal (AFT)
entries.what: Service matters and court-martial appeals of the armed forces.

entries.name: National Green Tribunal (NGT)
entries.what: Environmental cases.

entries.name: Securities Appellate Tribunal (SAT)
entries.what: Appeals from orders of the securities, insurance and pension regulators.
entries.law: Securities and Exchange Board of India Act, 1992

entries.name: Debts Recovery Tribunals (DRT) and Appellate Tribunals (DRAT)
entries.what: Recovery of debts due to banks and financial institutions.
entries.law: Recovery of Debts and Bankruptcy Act, 1993

entries.name: Telecom Disputes Settlement and Appellate Tribunal (TDSAT)
entries.what: Telecom, broadcasting and related disputes.
entries.law: Telecom Regulatory Authority of India Act, 1997

entries.name: Appellate Tribunal for Electricity (APTEL)
entries.what: Appeals from the electricity regulatory commissions.

entries.name: Consumer Commissions (District, State, National)
entries.what: Consumer complaints: the District Commission, the State Commission and the National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission (NCDRC).

entries.name: Real Estate Regulatory Authorities and Appellate Tribunals
entries.what: Complaints of home buyers against promoters and agents. Each State and Union Territory has its own authority and website.

entries.name: Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal (MACT)
entries.what: Compensation claims for motor accidents; usually held by a District or Additional District Judge.

entries.name: Labour Courts and Industrial Tribunals
entries.what: Industrial and labour disputes.
entries.law: The labour law in force (check the current Act)

entries.name: Railway Claims Tribunal
entries.what: Claims against the railways for loss of goods, refunds and accident compensation.

entries.name: eCourts (district and taluka courts)
entries.what: Case status, cause lists and orders of district and taluka courts across India, by CNR number, party name or case number.

entries.name: National Judicial Data Grid (NJDG)
entries.what: Counts of pending and decided cases in the district courts and High Courts.

entries.name: Supreme Court of India website
entries.what: Case status, cause lists, judgments, rules, circulars and e-filing of the Supreme Court.

entries.name: Department of Justice
entries.what: The Government of India department for the administration of justice, legal aid schemes and judicial infrastructure.

entries.name: Ministry of Law and Justice
entries.what: The Ministry, with its Department of Legal Affairs and Legislative Department.

entries.name: Law Commission of India
entries.what: Reports recommending changes to the law.

entries.name: National Portal of India
entries.what: The Government of India's entry point to ministries, States and services.

entries.name: India Code (central and State Acts)
entries.what: The official collection of central Acts and of State Acts, with the rules, regulations and notifications made under them. Use it to find a bare Act and its subordinate legislation.
entries.note: VIDHI does not copy India Code text: written permission is needed first.

entries.name: Legislative Department
entries.what: The department that drafts central legislation; publishes new Acts and Ordinances.

entries.name: e-Gazette (Gazette of India)
entries.what: The official gazette: every central Act, rule, regulation and notification as published, with its date. The authoritative place to check when a provision came into force.

entries.name: Digital Sansad (Parliament of India)
entries.what: Bills, debates and committee reports of Parliament.
entries.note: No address is shown: Parliament's site is not on a government domain and no official page linking to it could be confirmed by the checker.

entries.name: State Acts, rules and gazettes
entries.what: State Acts are on India Code under each State. The State's own gazette and Law Department site publish its rules and notifications; the State High Court's site publishes the civil and criminal rules of practice for the courts under it.
entries.note: No State gazette address is listed here: none has been checked yet.

entries.name: Judgments and Orders portal (Supreme Court and High Courts)
entries.what: The official free-text search of judgments and orders of the Supreme Court and the High Courts.

entries.name: Supreme Court Reports (SCR), the official reporter
entries.what: The Supreme Court's own law report. The Court publishes it in digital form (e-SCR). A citation has the form [year] volume S.C.R. page.

entries.name: Supreme Court Cases (SCC)
entries.what: A widely cited private law report of Supreme Court judgments, published by Eastern Book Company; available in print and on SCC OnLine by subscription. A citation has the form (year) volume SCC page.
entries.note: A commercial publication, not an official source. VIDHI has no connection with it and does not copy from it.

entries.name: All India Reporter (AIR)
entries.what: A long-running private law report covering the Supreme Court and the High Courts. A citation has the form AIR year court page (for example SC for the Supreme Court).
entries.note: A commercial publication, not an official source. VIDHI has no connection with it and does not copy from it.

entries.name: Neutral citations
entries.what: The courts' own citation given to each judgment, independent of any publisher, in the form year INSC number for the Supreme Court. Where a judgment has one, it can be used to find the judgment on the court's own site.

entries.name: High Court websites
entries.what: Each High Court publishes its own judgments, orders and cause lists. See the list of High Court websites.

entries.name: Judgments in VIDHI
entries.what: VIDHI's Judgments page searches the public case list of the Supreme Court and the 25 High Courts. Every record there is labelled as not reviewed: read the court's own copy before relying on it.

entries.name: Supreme Court Rules, 2013
entries.what: The rules of practice and procedure of the Supreme Court, with the forms for petitions and appeals. Published on the Supreme Court's website.

entries.name: High Court Rules (Original Side and Appellate Side) and filing formats
entries.what: Each High Court makes its own rules for the High Court and the civil and criminal rules of practice for the courts under it, and publishes its registry's filing checklists. They are on that High Court's website.

entries.name: e-Filing (district courts and High Courts)
entries.what: The eCourts e-filing service, with its user manuals for filing cases and documents online.

entries.name: NALSA Handbook of Formats
entries.what: Formats published by the National Legal Services Authority for legal aid work.

entries.name: National Legal Services Authority (NALSA)
entries.what: The national body for free legal aid. A person who needs a lawyer and cannot afford one can apply to the legal services authorities. VIDHI is a tool for lawyers and does not represent anyone.

entries.name: NALSA legal aid helpline: 15100
entries.what: The national toll-free legal aid helpline number, as published on NALSA's website.

entries.name: Apply for legal aid online
entries.what: The legal aid application form of the legal services authorities.

entries.name: Supreme Court Legal Services Committee (SCLSC)
entries.what: Legal aid for cases in the Supreme Court.

entries.name: State Legal Services Authorities (SLSA)
entries.what: Every State and Union Territory has a State Legal Services Authority. Choose a State to see its authority's website and office phone, as listed in NALSA's directory.

entries.name: District Legal Services Authorities (DLSA) and Taluk Legal Services Committees
entries.what: Every district has a District Legal Services Authority, usually at the district court complex, and talukas have Taluk Legal Services Committees. The State authority's website lists them.

entries.name: Tele-Law
entries.what: The Department of Justice's service for legal advice by phone or video through Common Service Centres.

entries.name: Bare Acts
entries.what: The text of an Act without commentary. The official text is on India Code and in the Gazette; printed bare Acts are sold by several publishers.

entries.name: Commentaries
entries.what: Section-by-section books on an Act, with the cases under each section. Which commentary is suitable is for the lawyer to judge; VIDHI recommends none.

entries.name: Legal encyclopedias and digests
entries.what: Encyclopedias state the law subject by subject (for example Halsbury's Laws of India); digests collect short notes of cases by topic and year.

entries.name: Online legal databases
entries.what: Subscription databases (such as SCC OnLine and Manupatra) and free ones (such as Indian Kanoon) index judgments and Acts. They are private services, not official sources: confirm a judgment against the court's own copy.

entries.name: VIDHI's own law library
entries.what: The Acts loaded in VIDHI are drafts that no lawyer has reviewed yet. They are for looking up, not for relying on.
